newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan major killed in border clash with India.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan major killed in border clash with India.

text.p: A Pakistan army major was killed in a clash with an Indian border force overnight in the disputed region of Kashmir, a Pakistan military statement said on Wednesday.
The Indians also suffered casualties but their number was not known, said the statement.
It was the most serious border clash for several months between arch-rivals India and Pakistan, currently preparing for a second round in recently-resumed peace talks.

The statement said the clash followed "unprovoked firing" by the Indian Border Security Force (BSF) on civilians building an embankment on the Pakistani side of what it called the working boundary with the Indian-ruled part of disputed Kashmir.

"Pakistan (paramilitary) Rangers personnel moved in support of the civilians and, during exchange of fire, Major Jamil of Pakistan Rangers embraced Shahadat (martyrdom)," the Pakistani statement said.
"Pakistan Rangers retaliated, inflicting casualties on the BSF," the statement said. "However, the number of Indian casualties could not be ascertained."

The official APP news agency quoted a spokesman for the Inter-Services Public Relations department as saying that Indian security forces had fired on civilians and Rangers in the past in an attempt to alter the status of the working boundary.

He said a protest had been lodged with a United Nations military observers group for India and Pakistan, and the Foreign Ministry had also summoned the Indian High Commissioner in Islamabad to convey Pakistan's "serious concern" over the latest incident.
"Vigilance is being maintained by Pakistan Rangers along the working boundary," the spokesman said.
Tension has run high between the two sides during more than seven years of a separatist revolt in the two-thirds of Kashmir ruled by India.
Pakistan controls the remaining third of the region, over which the two countries have fought two of their three wars since independence from Britain in 1947.
Top Indian and Pakistani foreign ministry officials met in New Delhi in March, marking a resumption of the dialogue between the two countries after a three-year deadlock over Kashmir.
Pakistan has proposed the next round in Islamabad be held on June 19-22, but still awaits Indian approval of the dates.
